commentary: DCE iron ore futures rose in early trading before pulling back slightly. The most-traded contract I2601 hit a high of 804.5 and ﬁnally closed at 800.5, up 0.5% from the previous working day. Traders sold at market prices; steel mills held a bearish outlook on future ore prices, showing moderate purchase willingness. Market trading acƟvity was moderate. In Shandong, PB ﬁnes traded at 796-800 yuan, ﬂat from yesterday's price; in Hebei, PB ﬁnes traded at 803-813 yuan/mt, basically ﬂat from the previous day. According to SMM staƟsƟcs, this week (November 29 to December 5), the impact from blast furnace maintenance on hot metal producƟon was 1.5412 million mt, up 89,900 mt WoW. Next week (December 6 to December 12), the impact from blast furnace maintenance on hot metal producƟon is expected to be 1.6224 million mt, an increase of 81,200 mt WoW. Hot metal producƟon is on a downward trend, and the weakening fundamentals are weighing on ore prices. However, with an important domesƟc conference approaching, the market sƟll holds certain expectaƟons. Market senƟment remains posiƟve, and ore prices remain relaƟvely ﬁrm.
